rules.title: Massachusetts Security Deposit Law - Remedies and Transfer Requirements
rules.requirement: If a landlord fails to properly handle a security deposit (e.g., not depositing it in a required account, not returning it on time, or not transferring it to a new owner), the tenant can be awarded triple damages plus interest, court costs, and attorney's fees. Landlords who sell the property must transfer the deposit (or last month's rent) to the new owner and notify the tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential tenancies in Massachusetts where a security deposit or last month's rent advance was collected.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to vacation or recreational leases of 100 days or less.
rules.quoted_span: If the lessor or his agent fails to comply with clauses (a), (d), or (e) of subsection 6, the tenant shall be awarded damages in an amount equal to three times the amount of such security deposit or balance thereof to which the tenant is entitled plus interest at the rate of five per cent from the date when such payment became due, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the lease is a vacation/recreational tenancy of 100 days or less
